Chung Ho Park, partner and head of Korea at KKR (Image: KKR)

AI-driven dealmaking leads today’s Asia Pacific headlines as US private equity firm KKR pours a record $3 billion into South Korea’s data centre and power sectors. Also in the news are Mapletree Logistics Trust selling a Shanghai asset for $48 million and BDx Data Centers breaking ground on a 640-megawatt campus in Indonesia.

KKR Eyes More Korea Deals After Record $3B AI Push

KKR has ploughed roughly $3 billion into South Korea this year, a record tally, and expects more deals as the country’s role in the global AI supply chain drives demand for data centres and power, Bloomberg calculated.

The tally includes a roughly $2.2 billion stake with IMM Investment and Stonebridge in SK Horizon, a data centre platform spun off from SK Telecom, and a $1.3 billion renewable venture with SK Inc powering AI facilities and chipmakers. Read more>>

Mapletree Logistics Trust Selling Shanghai Warehouse Park for $48M

Singapore-listed Mapletree Logistics Trust has agreed to sell a Shanghai warehouse park for RMB 323 million ($48.2 million), the REIT’s manager said. The property spans two phases totalling 37,558 square metres (404,274 square feet).

The price matches an independent March 2026 valuation, and proceeds will fund investment in more modern logistics assets, the manager said. Acquired in 2008, the property is among recent disposals trimming MLT’s portfolio to 168 properties once the sale completes. Read more>>

Singapore’s BDx Breaks Ground on 640MW Indonesia Data Centre Campus

Singapore-based BDx Data Centers has broken ground on a 640-megawatt AI data centre campus in West Java, a two-hour drive from Jakarta. The Jatiluhur project, CGK4, secured 845 megavolt-amperes of grid capacity from state utility PLN, BDx said.

BDx secured a $320 million loan this year for its Indonesian expansion, spanning three AI campuses with over 1.2 gigavolt-amperes of grid capacity. CGK4’s first 120MW building is due online in early 2027, using direct-to-chip liquid cooling, BDx said. Read more>>

Apollo Provides $585M in Financing to The Executive Centre

Apollo-managed funds and other investors have provided $585 million in financing to The Executive Centre, one of Asia’s largest flexible office operators, Apollo said. Proceeds will refinance debt and fund TEC’s expansion across its 260-plus centres.

The deal extends Apollo’s track record of hybrid deals in Asia, including with JSW Cement, Global Schools Group and Hero FinCorp, the firm said. A&O Shearman advised Apollo, while Clifford Chance and Rippledot Capital advised TEC. Read more>>

Microsoft to Expand Taiwan Data Centres From Two to Four Sites

Microsoft plans to expand its two Taiwan data centres to four amid AI demand that it expects to outstrip supply for two more years, said Sean Pien, general manager of Microsoft Taiwan.

The Taoyuan facilities serve regulated clients including government, finance and healthcare, and have expanded offerings from about 70 to over 200 services, Pien said. Taiwan remains central to global AI supply chains, spanning server production, compute and storage, with no near-term relocation risk, he added. Read more>>

Mitsubishi Raises Ayala Stake to 20% for $762M

Japanese trading house Mitsubishi Corp will raise its stake in Philippine conglomerate Ayala Corp to 20 percent from 5.4 percent for JPY 120 billion ($762 million), betting on the country’s growth, Mitsubishi said.

The tie-up deepens Mitsubishi’s exposure to Ayala Land, the group’s property arm and one of the Philippines’ largest developers, part of a push into real estate and energy. Read more>>

Futu Doubles Hong Kong Office Space at Pacific Place

Hong Kong-based Futu Securities has opened a 42,000 square foot (3,902 square metre) office at Pacific Place, doubling its United Centre space, the company said. Its Hong Kong office space now totals over 70,000 square feet.

The office houses a Private Wealth Center for high-net-worth clients and backs plans to hire 2,000 staff over five years, Futu said. Read more>>

Australia’s Victoria Bans Data Centres From Residential Zones

Victoria, home to Melbourne and one of Australia’s largest states, has banned new data centres from residential areas and will require them to supply their own renewable energy, addressing rising community pushback, the state government said.

While data centres remain vital to the economy, Victoria said operators must limit strain on local water and power resources. The move follows a national push where most states agreed in August to offset data centre power demand with new renewables. Read more>>
